haiku-low.q1: After the Message Store transaction commits (message and outbox row written together). The ack carries msg_id and seq. It never waits for any recipient.
haiku-low.q2: The sender gets an error and nothing is fanned out, since no outbox row exists. The retry must reuse the same client_msg_id, which the unique key enforces.
haiku-low.q3: After 30 seconds with no heartbeat. Heartbeats come every 10 seconds and refresh the Presence Store key, whose TTL is 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q4: It is treated as offline for that message: an inbox entry is written, the backlog flag is set, and one best-effort push is sent.
haiku-low.q5: It is ignored. Push is never retried, and a failure never touches the inbox or the Message Store.
haiku-low.q6: Inbox entries are sent in (conversation, seq) order, one at a time, and deleted only after client ack. Clients drop duplicates by message id.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row is written in the same transaction as the message. The relay publishes unpublished rows on restart and retries until published, so no acked message is lost.
haiku-low.q8: In the Presence Store: one key per user holding user-to-node, with a 30-second TTL. The entry is removed when the key expires after 30 seconds without a heartbeat.
haiku-low.q9: A worker looks up presence and sends an RPC to the recipient's gateway, which pushes over WebSocket. The client's ack within 5 seconds confirms arrival.
haiku-low.q10: In the Offline Inbox, keyed (user, conv, seq). It is written when the recipient is offline, flagged, unreachable, or unacked in 5 seconds. Entries are deleted on client ack or expire after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: The Offline Inbox, read ordered by (conv, seq). Each entry holds a message id, and the message body is read from the Message Store.
haiku-low.q12: The job is redelivered and reprocessed from the start. Some recipients may get the message again, and clients drop duplicates. Inbox writes are idempotent on (user, conv, seq).

sonnet.q1: After the message and outbox row commit in one transaction in the Message Store. The ack carries (msg_id, seq). It never waits for any recipient.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error. No outbox row exists, so nothing is fanned out and no one receives it. The retry must carry the same client_msg_id (same conversation), so the unique key returns the original or does the first write.
sonnet.q3: After 30 s with no heartbeat (heartbeat every 10 s; the Presence key TTL is 30 s and expires).
sonnet.q4: It is treated as offline for that message: an inbox entry is written, the backlog flag is set, and one best-effort push is sent. If the client did get it, the later duplicate is dropped by message id.
sonnet.q5: It is ignored. The push is never retried and never affects the inbox or Message Store.
sonnet.q6: In order by (conv, seq). The drain loops until the inbox is empty. Duplicates are dropped by the client by message id (at-least-once).
sonnet.q7: The outbox row, written in the same transaction as the message. If the process crashes before publish, the row stays unpublished and the relay publishes it on restart. The relay retries until it succeeds.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Store, a key-value store with one key per user mapping the user to a gateway node. The 30 s TTL expires the key when heartbeats stop (each heartbeat refreshes it).
sonnet.q9: The worker looks up presence and the backlog flag, then makes an RPC to the recipient's gateway node. The gateway pushes it over the WebSocket. The client's ack, within 5 s, confirms arrival.
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox, keyed (user, conv, seq), with the message id as the value. It is written when the recipient is offline, has a backlog flag, the RPC fails, or there is no ack in 5 s. An entry is removed when the client acks it during a drain, or by the 30-day TTL.
sonnet.q11: The gateway reads the user's Offline Inbox, ordered by (conv, seq). The bodies are read from the Message Store, since the inbox holds only the message id.
sonnet.q12: The job is not acked, so it is redelivered and reprocessed from the start. Recipients who already got the message may get it again, and clients dedup. Inbox writes are idempotent, and push is sent only when the inbox insert was new.
